taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Kenpoly-convocation-arena, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1434 | 2.5 | 2.5
2 | 1879 | 5.42 | 7.92
3 | 318 | 18 | 25.9
4 | 3488 | 24.3 | 50.2
5 | 542 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Kenpoly-convocation-arena, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station Kenpoly-convocation-arena, Bori Metropolis**

The interpreted VES model comprises five layers. Resistivity increases from Layer 1 (1434 Ω·m) to Layer 2 (1879 Ω·m), then drops sharply to a low-resistivity Layer 3 (318 Ω·m, 18 m thick), rises markedly to a resistive Layer 4 (3488 Ω·m), and finally decreases to Layer 5 (542 Ω·m, basement/substratum).

Applying the curve-type rule to successive triplets:
- Layers 1-2-3: 1434 < 1879 > 318 → K
- Layers 2-3-4: 1879 > 318 < 3488 → H
- Layers 3-4-5: 318 < 3488 > 542 → K

This yields a KHK-type curve, consistent with the classification on file. The sequence reflects an alternating resistive–conductive–resistive–conductive layering, typical of interbedded sand/clay units overlying a more conductive basal layer. Drilling teams should anticipate variable lithology with at least one significant low-resistivity (possibly clayey or saturated) zone at depth (Layer 3) before encountering a resistive unit (Layer 4) and a final conductive layer (Layer 5).

{"curve_type_stated": "KHK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
